- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% to align with sentiment.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.01 to 0.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match recent 5-day average for smoother transition.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent peak, model often overcorrects downward; apply upward bias of 1–2% to prevent premature mean reversion.
